summary.one_liner: Curlie is a command-line frontend to curl that offers HTTPie-style syntax and pretty output while keeping all of curl's options.
summary.what_it_does: Curlie wraps curl and exposes all of its options with a simpler HTTPie-like syntax (method, URL, and items). It pretty-prints JSON output when run interactively, and pretty-printing can be forced with --pretty. Headers are written to stderr rather than stdout, as in curl. Output is streamed and formatted on the fly rather than buffered, which helps when debugging streamed data. The --curl option prints the equivalent curl command that was executed. The README also describes a goreleaser-based build for testing cross-platform compilation.
use_cases: make HTTP requests from the terminal with simpler syntax
send JSON data with custom headers
inspect the underlying curl command for a request
test APIs with curl features and HTTPie-style ergonomics
notable: HTTPie-style syntax on top of full curl option support
Pretty-printed JSON output when run interactively
--curl option prints the executed curl command
Headers go to stderr and output is not buffered
Installable via Homebrew, Go, Scoop, MacPorts, pkg, mise, and binary downloads
caveats: README usage section has no examples shown (the code blocks for simple GET and custom requests are missing)
Differs from HTTPie in that headers go to stderr rather than stdout
